# SearchFn Documentation

> Full-text search engine and adapter system for TypeScript, Python, and Swift. Ships a built-in BM25 engine for in-process and browser-persistent search, plus thin adapters for Postgres, Meilisearch, Elasticsearch, and OpenSearch.

This document is intended for large language models and agentic developer tools. It contains an outline of the SearchFn documentation with deep-links to each page; for the full content see `llms-full.txt`.

## Ai Resources

- [Claude Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/claude): Use SearchFn effectively with Claude Code and Claude Projects.
- [Codex Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/codex): Use SearchFn with OpenAI Codex CLI and Codex agents.
- [Cursor Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/cursor): Pin SearchFn docs in Cursor and prompt the agent effectively.
- [llms.txt and llms-full.txt](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/llms-txt): Plain-text documentation feeds for AI coding tools.
- [MCP Server](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/mcp): Connect Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients to SearchFn documentation.
- [Skills](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources/skills): Factory Droid skills for SearchFn setup, indexing, and adapter selection.

## Top Level

- [AI Resources](https://searchfn.com/docs/ai-resources): Use SearchFn with AI coding tools — Cursor, Claude, Codex, Windsurf, and any LLM that consumes llms.txt.
- [Architecture](https://searchfn.com/docs/architecture): Built-in search engine, package layers, adapter contract, and response semantics.
- [Comparison](https://searchfn.com/docs/comparison): SearchFn vs Algolia, Typesense, Meilisearch direct, Elasticsearch direct, Postgres FTS direct, FlexSearch, MiniSearch, Lunr.js, Orama, Pagefind.
- [Examples](https://searchfn.com/docs/examples): Runnable example apps shipped with SearchFn.
- [Getting Started with Swift](https://searchfn.com/docs/getting-started-swift): Build local Swift search with the standalone SearchFn Swift package.
- [Getting Started](https://searchfn.com/docs/getting-started): Install SearchFn, index documents, and run your first search query in minutes.
- [SearchFn](https://searchfn.com/docs): A full-text search engine and adapter system for TypeScript applications.
- [Quickstart](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart): Get SearchFn indexing and serving queries in 5–10 minutes for your stack.
- [Recipes](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes): Copy-pasteable patterns for the things you actually want to do with SearchFn.

## Documentation

- [Migrating Between Adapters](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/advanced/adapter-migration): Move from Memory → Postgres → Meilisearch → Elasticsearch without downtime.
- [Writing an Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/advanced/writing-an-adapter): Implement SearchAdapter against your own backend — full guide.
- [Diagnostics](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple/diagnostics): Opt-in event sink for observing SearchFn lifecycle on Apple.
- [Apple Runtime](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple): SearchFn on iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS — standalone Swift package.
- [Memory Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple/memory-adapter): SearchFnMemoryAdapter — in-process, ephemeral, fastest.
- [Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple/setup): Add SearchFn to a Swift project.
- [SQLite Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple/sqlite-adapter): SearchFnSQLiteAdapter — persistent on-device search backed by SQLite.
- [SwiftUI](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/apple/swiftui): Bind SearchFn results into a SwiftUI view.
- [WASM Core](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core-wasm): Rust+WebAssembly build of the SearchFn engine — experimental, for workloads where the JS engine isn't fast enough.
- [WASM Core Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core-wasm/setup): Install and use the WASM engine.
- [When to Use the WASM Core](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core-wasm/when-to-use): Pick WASM over the TS engine — or pick neither.
- [BM25 Scoring](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core/bm25): The formula, the constants, and when to tune them.
- [Customization](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core/customization): Replace any pipeline stage — tokenizer, normalizer, stop words, stemmer.
- [Fuzzy Matching](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core/fuzzy): How SearchFn handles typos — Levenshtein distance with vocabulary expansion.
- [Core Engine](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core): Inside @searchfn/core — the full-text engine that powers MemoryAdapter and IndexedDbAdapter.
- [Inverted Index](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core/inverted-index): How SearchFn stores postings — in memory, in IndexedDB, and what that means for performance.
- [Text Pipeline](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/core/pipeline): How SearchFn turns raw field text into searchable tokens.
- [Deploy: Cloudflare Workers](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/cloudflare-workers): SearchFn on Cloudflare Workers — what works and what doesn't.
- [Deploy: Docker](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/docker): Containerize SearchFn — multi-stage build, production image, compose for local stack.
- [Deploy: Fly.io](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/fly): SearchFn on Fly with Postgres, Meilisearch, or a self-hosted Elasticsearch sidecar.
- [Deploy](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy): Where to run SearchFn — the tradeoffs per platform.
- [Deploy: Kubernetes](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/kubernetes): Deployment, Service, Ingress, and HPA for SearchFn — production-shaped.
- [Deploy: Railway](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/railway): SearchFn on Railway with Railway Postgres or external Meilisearch.
- [Scaling](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/scaling): Capacity planning, bottlenecks, and how to scale a SearchFn deployment.
- [Deploy: Vercel](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/deploy/vercel): Run SearchFn server-side on Vercel using Next.js API routes or serverless functions.
- [Cache Tuning](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/performance/cache-tuning): LRU caches in the built-in engine, OS cache for Postgres, and how to size both.
- [Performance](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/performance): Where to look when SearchFn is slow.
- [Indexing Throughput](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/performance/indexing-throughput): Make backfills and bulk indexing fast.
- [Query Latency](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/performance/query-latency): Where the milliseconds go and how to claw them back.
- [HTTP Mount](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/python/http-mount): Mount the SearchFn routes on FastAPI, Starlette, or Flask.
- [Python](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/python): SearchFn Python — a lightweight DataFn companion for database-backed full-text search.
- [Indexing](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/python/indexing): How index_data walks DataFn models and populates the inverted index.
- [Search](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/python/search): How search_index ranks records and what to expect from the Python scoring model.
- [Setup](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/python/setup): Install searchfn (Python) and wire it to your DataFn schema.
- [Security](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security): The threat model and defense layers for a SearchFn deployment.
- [Multi-Tenant Isolation](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security/multi-tenant-isolation): Stop tenants from leaking into each other's search results.
- [Payload Limits](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security/payload-limits): How SearchFn caps request size, query length, and batch counts — and why.
- [Production Checklist](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security/production-checklist): Pre-launch audit for a SearchFn deployment.
- [Request Authorization](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security/request-authz): The authorize callback — how to write one, how to test it.
- [Secret Redaction](https://searchfn.com/docs/documentation/security/secret-redaction): What SearchFn strips from log output — and what you still have to handle.

## Quickstart

- [Bun](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/bun): SearchFn on Bun's native HTTP server.
- [Express](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/express): Mount SearchFn into an Express app in under 10 minutes.
- [FastAPI](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/fastapi): Mount the Python SearchFn server inside a FastAPI app.
- [Fastify](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/fastify): SearchFn on Fastify with a single route registration.
- [Flask](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/flask): Mount SearchFn into a Flask app.
- [Hono](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/hono): SearchFn on Hono with the Memory adapter for dev and Postgres for prod.
- [Next.js](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/nextjs): SearchFn in Next.js (App Router) — server route for search + IndexedDB on the client.
- [Starlette](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/starlette): Mount SearchFn into a Starlette app.
- [SvelteKit](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/sveltekit): SearchFn in a SvelteKit app — IndexedDB on the client, Postgres on the server.
- [Swift](https://searchfn.com/docs/quickstart/swift): SearchFn on iOS, macOS, watchOS — in-memory or SQLite-backed local search.

## Recipes

- [AuthFn Integration](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/authfn-integration): Wire SearchFn's authorize callback to AuthFn sessions and roles.
- [Autocomplete](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/autocomplete): Search-as-you-type with prefix matching and low latency.
- [Backfill From An Existing Database](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/backfill-from-db): Populate SearchFn from Postgres, MySQL, or Mongo without re-fetching everything twice.
- [Cross-Resource Ranking](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/cross-resource-ranking): Search across products, articles, and users — and rank them fairly.
- [DataFn Integration (Deep)](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/datafn-integration): Wire SearchFn as a DataFn search provider — server, client, native, and dataflows.
- [FileFn Integration](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/filefn-integration): Index FileFn file metadata and extracted text content into SearchFn.
- [Hybrid Local + Remote Search](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/hybrid-local-remote): IndexedDB for hot data on the client; server search for everything else.
- [Index Snapshot and Restore](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/index-snapshot-restore): Capture the SearchFn index state for backup, fixtures, or seeding new environments.
- [Multi-Language Search](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/multi-language): Per-language stop words, stemming, and tokenization.
- [Multi-Tenant Search](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/multi-tenant): Keep tenants' search results isolated — even when sharing infrastructure.
- [Partial Reindex](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/partial-reindex): Re-index only the records that changed since the last sync.
- [Reindex With No Downtime](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/reindex-no-downtime): Blue-green index swap — never serve a half-rebuilt index.
- [Relevance Testing](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/relevance-testing): Make search quality measurable, not anecdotal.
- [Snippet Highlighting](https://searchfn.com/docs/recipes/snippet-highlighting): Return matched fragments with the hit terms wrapped in HTML mark tags.

## Reference

- [Elasticsearch / OpenSearch Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters/elastic-opensearch): Elastic-compatible adapter for Elasticsearch and OpenSearch clusters.
- [Adapters](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters): Choose the right search adapter — built-in engine or external backend.
- [IndexedDB Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters/indexeddb): Browser-persistent full-text search using SearchFn's built-in engine with IndexedDB storage.
- [Meilisearch Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters/meilisearch): External Meilisearch adapter for hosted or self-hosted search backends.
- [Memory Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters/memory): In-process full-text search using SearchFn's built-in engine.
- [Postgres Adapter](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/adapters/postgres): Production-grade full-text search using Postgres tsvector.
- [Capabilities](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/capabilities): Per-adapter feature matrix.
- [Changelog](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/changelog): Release notes for SearchFn packages.
- [Client API](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/client): Create and configure a SearchFn client for in-app search.
- [Configuration](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/configuration): Full configuration tables for the server, client, and every adapter.
- [Envelopes](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/envelopes): Canonical SearchFn request and response envelopes.
- [Errors](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/errors): All SearchFn error codes — cause, fix, and retry semantics.
- [Events](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/events): Server log events and Swift diagnostics events.
- [Python Reference](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/python): API reference for the Python SearchFn package.
- [Server API](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/server): Expose SearchFn as an HTTP API with authorization, logging, and secret redaction.
- [Swift Package Reference](https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/swift): Reference for the standalone SearchFn Swift package, adapters, convenience APIs, and diagnostics.
